editorial:
Imagine working a grueling night shift and being so tired that you can barely keep your eyes open. That is exactly where you find Tom, a guy whose wife keeps warning him that he is pushing himself too hard. She tells him that if he does not get some real sleep, his brain will start playing tricks on him. Instead of taking a nap, Tom decides to head out into the woods for a camping trip to clear his head. The vibe is super creepy from the start because you can tell he is not thinking straight, and the quiet woods make every little sound feel like a threat.

You will really dig how the movie plays with your head, making you wonder if the monsters are real or just side effects of sleep deprivation. The acting is solid and the pacing keeps you on edge without feeling rushed. One downside is that some parts move a bit slow, but the payoff is worth it. If you love psychological scares, you should definitely check this out. It looks amazing streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: You find out that the monsters Tom saw were not real creatures, but hallucinations caused by his lack of sleep. The big twist is that Tom actually hurt people in the woods while he was dreaming. In the final scene, he wakes up to realize he has been sleepwalking the entire time. He ends up trapped in a loop of madness, unable to tell what is real and what is a dream as the screen fades to black.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves movies that mess with your mind and make you question reality.
